summary: On three kinds of days the Kohanim say Birkas Kohanim four times in one day: on fast days, on the days of the maamados, and on Yom Kippur.

chunks.en: Three times a year the Kohanim lift
chunks.st: At three times in the year priests raise their hands

chunks.en: their hands four times in one day,
chunks.explain: To bless the people with Birkas Kohanim.
chunks.st: to recite the Priestly Benediction four times in a single day,

chunks.en: at Shacharis, at Mussaf, at Mincha, and at the closing of the gates,
chunks.st: in the morning prayer, in the additional prayer, in the afternoon prayer, and in the evening in the closing of the gates, i.e., the ne’ila prayer. And these are the three times:

words.note: Ne'ilah, the last tefillah at the end of the day.

chunks.en: on fast days, at the maamados, and on Yom Kippur.
chunks.explain: The maamados are explained in the next mishnah.
chunks.st: During communal fasts held due to lack of rain, on which the closing prayer is recited; and during non-priestly watches [ma’amadot], when the Israelite members of the guard parallel to the priestly watch come and read the act of Creation from the Torah, as explained below; and on Yom Kippur.

words.note: Groups of regular Jews who stood for all of Yisrael while the korbanos were brought.

summary: Every Jew has a share in the daily korbanos, so groups called maamados stood for everyone. When a mishmar of Kohanim went up to Yerushalayim, its Yisraelim gathered at home and read the story of Creation.

chunks.en: These are the maamados:
chunks.st: These are the non-priestly watches:

chunks.st: Since it is stated: “

chunks.st: Command the children of Israel and say to them:

chunks.st: My offering of food, which is presented to Me made by a fire, of a sweet savor to Me, you shall guard the sacrifice to Me in its due season” (Numbers 28:2),

chunks.en: The early Neviim set up twenty-four mishmaros.
chunks.explain: Each mishmar was a group of Kohanim who took turns serving.
chunks.st: The mishna explains: Since it is impossible for the entire nation to be present in Jerusalem when the daily offering is brought, the early prophets, Samuel and David, instituted the division of the priests into twenty-four priestly watches,
chunks.stMore: each of which served for approximately one week, twice per year.

chunks.en: For each and every mishmar there was
chunks.st: For each and every priestly watch there was

chunks.en: a maamad in Yerushalayim, of Kohanim,
chunks.st: a corresponding non-priestly watch in Jerusalem of priests,

chunks.en: of Leviim,
chunks.st: Levites,

chunks.en: and of Yisraelim.
chunks.st: and Israelites
chunks.stMore: who would stand by the communal offerings for that day to represent the community.

chunks.en: When the time came for the mishmar to go up,
chunks.st: When the time arrived for the members of a certain priestly watch to ascend, the

chunks.en: the Kohanim and Leviim go up to Yerushalayim,
chunks.st: priests and Levites of that watch would ascend to Jerusalem to perform the Temple service.

chunks.en: and the Yisraelim of that mishmar gather
chunks.st: And as for the Israelites assigned to that priestly watch, some of them went up to Jerusalem, while the rest of them

chunks.en: in their towns and read the story of Creation.
chunks.st: assembled in their towns and read the act of Creation.

summary: The men of the maamad fasted from Monday to Thursday, and each day they read a part of the story of Creation from the Torah.

chunks.en: The men of the maamad would fast
chunks.st: And the members of the non-priestly watch, who represented the entire community that week, would fast

chunks.en: four days a week,
chunks.st: four days a week,

chunks.en: from Monday until Thursday.
chunks.st: from Monday until Thursday.

chunks.en: They did not fast on Erev Shabbos,
chunks.st: And they would not fast on Shabbat eve,

chunks.en: in honor of Shabbos.
chunks.st: in deference to Shabbat,
chunks.stMore: as they did not wish to start Shabbat while fasting.

chunks.en: And not on Sunday,
chunks.st: And they did not fast on Sunday,

chunks.en: so that they would not go from rest
chunks.st: so as not to go from rest

chunks.en: and delight to hard work and fasting, and die.

chunks.st: and delight immediately to exertion and fasting, and run the risk that they might die as a result of the abrupt change.

summary: Nine families each had a special day to bring wood for the mizbe'ach. On Rosh Chodesh Teves there was no maamad, because there were so many other special things that day.

chunks.en: The times for the wood of the Kohanim and the people were nine.
chunks.explain: Families gave wood for the mizbe'ach, each on its own day.
chunks.st: The mishna details the times for the wood offering of priests and the people. These were private holidays specific to certain families, on which their members would volunteer a wood offering for the altar. There were nine such days and families:

chunks.en: On the first of Nisan,
chunks.st: On the first of Nisan,

chunks.en: the family of Arach ben Yehudah.
chunks.st: the descendants of Araḥ ben Yehuda;

chunks.en: On the twentieth of Tammuz,
chunks.st: on the twentieth of Tammuz,

chunks.en: the family of Dovid ben Yehudah.
chunks.st: the descendants of David ben Yehuda;

chunks.en: On the fifth of Av,
chunks.st: on the fifth of Av,

chunks.en: the family of Parosh ben Yehudah.
chunks.st: the descendants of Parosh ben Yehuda;

chunks.en: On the seventh of it,
chunks.st: on the seventh of Av,

chunks.en: the family of Yonadav ben Reichav.
chunks.st: the descendants of Jonadab ben Rechab;

chunks.en: On the tenth of it,
chunks.st: on the tenth of Av,

chunks.st: who erred with regard to his tribe, i.e., Israelites who did not know which tribe they were from,

chunks.he: וּבְנֵי גוֹנְבֵי עֱלִי בְּנֵי קוֹצְעֵי קְצִיעוֹת.
chunks.en: and the families of the "pestle hiders" and the "fig cutters."
chunks.st: and the descendants of those who deceived the authorities with a pestle; and the descendants of those who packed dried figs.

chunks.st: On the twentieth of Av,

summary: Five sad things happened on the seventeenth of Tammuz, and five on Tishah B'Av, like the Beis HaMikdash being destroyed. From the start of Av, we have less simcha.
stIntro: The mishna discusses the five major communal fast days.

chunks.en: Five things happened to our fathers
chunks.st: Five calamitous matters occurred to our forefathers

chunks.en: on the seventeenth of Tammuz,
chunks.st: on the seventeenth of Tammuz,

chunks.en: and five on Tishah B'Av.
chunks.st: and five other disasters happened on the Ninth of Av.

chunks.en: On the seventeenth of Tammuz the Luchos were broken,
chunks.explain: Moshe broke them when he saw the golden calf.
chunks.st: On the seventeenth of Tammuz the tablets were broken
chunks.stMore: by Moses when he saw that the Jews had made the golden calf;

chunks.en: the korban Tamid stopped,
chunks.st: the daily offering was nullified by the Roman authorities and was never sacrificed again;

words.note: The korban brought every day, morning and afternoon.

chunks.en: the city was broken into,
chunks.explain: The walls of Yerushalayim were broken through.
chunks.st: the city walls of Jerusalem were breached;

chunks.en: Apostemos burned the Torah,
chunks.st: the general Apostemos publicly burned a Torah scroll;

chunks.en: and an idol was set up in the Heichal.
chunks.st: and Manasseh placed an idol in the Sanctuary.

chunks.en: that they would not go into Eretz Yisrael,
chunks.st: not enter Eretz Yisrael;

chunks.en: the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed the first time and the second time,

chunks.en: Beitar was captured,
chunks.st: and Beitar was captured;

chunks.en: and the city was plowed.
chunks.st: and the city of Jerusalem was plowed, as a sign that it would never be rebuilt.

chunks.en: When Av begins,
chunks.st: Not only does one fast on the Ninth of Av, but from when the month of Av begins,

chunks.en: we have less simcha.
chunks.st: one decreases acts of rejoicing.

summary: In the week of Tishah B'Av we do not cut hair or wash clothes. On Erev Tishah B'Av we eat a simple meal without meat or wine.

chunks.he: שַׁבָּת שֶׁחָל תִּשְׁעָה בְאָב לִהְיוֹת בְּתוֹכָהּ,
chunks.en: In the week that Tishah B'Av falls in,
chunks.st: During the week in which the Ninth of Av occurs,

chunks.en: it is forbidden to cut hair and to wash clothes,
chunks.st: it is prohibited to cut one’s hair and to launder clothes,

chunks.en: but on Thursday it is allowed, in honor of Shabbos.
chunks.explain: When Tishah B'Av falls on Friday.
chunks.st: but if the Ninth of Av occurs on a Friday, on Thursday these actions are permitted in deference to Shabbat.

chunks.en: On Erev Tishah B'Av a person should not
chunks.st: On the eve of the Ninth of Av

chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: One must adjust and decrease the amount he eats.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says one must turn over the bed,
chunks.explain: And sleep on the floor, like a mourner.
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda obligates one to overturn the bed and sleep on the floor like one in a state of mourning,

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: but the Sages did not agree with him.
chunks.st: but the Rabbis did not agree with him.
chunks.stMore: The mishna cites a passage that concludes its discussion of the month of Av, as well as the entire tractate of Ta’anit, on a positive note.

summary: The fifteenth of Av and Yom Kippur were the happiest days. The girls of Yerushalayim wore borrowed white clothes so no one would be embarrassed. The mishnah ends with the hope that the Beis HaMikdash will be built soon.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:

chunks.en: there were no days as happy for Yisrael
chunks.st: There were no days as joyous for the Jewish people

chunks.en: as the fifteenth of Av and Yom Kippur,
chunks.st: as the fifteenth of Av and as Yom Kippur,

chunks.en: when the girls of Yerushalayim would go out
chunks.st: as on them the daughters of Jerusalem would go out

chunks.en: in borrowed white clothes,
chunks.st: in white clothes, which each woman borrowed from another. Why were they borrowed? They did this

chunks.en: so as not to embarrass someone who has none.

chunks.explain: In case they had become tamei.

chunks.st: shall be praised” (Proverbs 31:30),
